items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There was Joe Thomas who played with Jimmie Lunceford... Jimmie Lunceford used to go in the Cotton Club.

ctx.x: Every city seems to have had some legendary figures, some great musicians who never left or never made it who are always recalled with great affection and admiration by people who knew them but were as good as the people we later go to know but for one reason or another circumstances prevented them from either leaving or making it. Were there any local legends like that you might tell us about?

Columbus? There was Joe Thomas who played with Jimmie Lunceford, he was from Columbus, OH. Sy Oliver, he stayed around Columbus, OH for years but his home was right outside of Columbus, OH. Not Youngstown, that’s too far. But he’s a Buckeye—everybody from Ohio they’re called Buckeyes—but he stayed around Columbus for years. Nancy Wilson is from Columbus, OH.
These are all people that made it. Were there any that were great musicians but for one reason or another never left?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: So did Jimmy Lunceford. ... I remember once we had done so many one-nighters and Jimmy Lunceford, you know, he had such a disciplined band.

ctx.x: No, I meant about the reading and everything? You could --

Yeah. Yeah, yeah, but it still wasn't -- you know, it took a lot of rehearsals to get what you wanted to get. And they had one guy, Chappie Willett, he used to write such hard arrangements it would take so long to get these players together. And musicians could read in those days, because Don Redman had a fantastic band. So did Duke. So did Jimmy Lunceford. So did Fletcher, Fletcher had a good band and he always wrote in the hard keys. That's why all the good musicians came out of Fletcher's band, you know.

In fact, all the musicians in those days were good musicians. They knew how to read. [But Basie's band was based on head arrangements because everybody took solos in Basie's band. Basie's band wasn't an ensemble band. It was noted for soloists, you know. Everybody was a fantastic soloist.]
